title: Resveratrol alleviates hippocampal oxidative stress, neuroinflammation and pyroptosis and reduces anxiety-like behavior in broilers under cold exposure.
abstract: Resveratrol (Res) exhibits antioxidant properties and neuroprotection. To investigate its protective effect, 576 one-day-old broilers were assigned to eight groups, reared under normal temperature or cold exposure (CE) and received the basal diet with 0, 250, 500, and 750 mg/kg Res, respectively. Broilers underwent behavioral tests, and hippocampus were collected. The results showed that after CE, the latency to first move and vocalise in open field test, induction times in tonic immobility test, and the latency to move, eat and vocalise in attention bias test were increased, while the numbers of movement steps and total vocalizations in attention bias test were decreased. Hematoxylin-eosin and Nissl staining displayed the perivascular aggregation of inflammatory cells and necrosis, disordered and sparse neurons, and reduced number of neurons in CE-broiler hippocampus. Transmission electron microscopy showed that CE caused synaptic terminals swelling and reduced the number of synaptic vesicles. Res restored abnormal changes in behaviors, histopathology and microstructure. CE decreased the CAT, T-SOD, GSH-px, and T-AOC activities, increased the H₂O₂ and MDA levels, upregulated the expression of genes and proteins related to inflammation (NF-κBp65, TNF-α, IL-2, IL-6, IL-8, IL-17) and pyroptosis (NLRP3, Caspase-1, GSDMD, ASC, IL-1β, IL-18), and depressed the expression of SIRT1 and BDNF/TrκB (CREB, FRS2, CRF, BRAF, PI3K) mRNA and proteins. Res normalized the abnormal expression in CE-broiler hippocampus. Overall, 500 mg/kg Res, an optimal supplementation dosage, relieved oxidative and inflammatory injuries by enhancing antioxidative capacity and inhibiting NF-κB signaling and NLRP3 inflammasome, alleviating anxiety-like behaviors in CE-broilers via modulating the SIRT1/BDNF/TrκB signaling.

title: EEG Resting-State Beta Band Dynamic Functional Connectivity Reveals State-Dependent Disruption of Language Network Lateralisation in First-Episode Schizophrenia.
abstract: Language disorganisation is a core feature of schizophrenia with significant functional consequences. However, its neurophysiological substrates remain poorly characterised, particularly in the early stages of the illness. This study investigated whether first-episode schizophrenia (FES) is associated with disruption in the organisation of language-network lateralisation, using both static and dynamic functional connectivity metrics in the EEG beta band. Thirty-one FES patients and 32 age-matched healthy volunteer subjects (HVS) underwent resting-state 64-channel EEG. Source-level connectivity was estimated using the weighted phase lag index with sliding windows, yielding 979 connectivity matrices per participant. Brain network states (BNS) were identified via k-means clustering. Static connectivity was obtained by time-averaging. Temporal features, graph-theoretical metrics, and language-network laterality indices were extracted for both whole-network and language-specific analyses. Group comparisons used permutation-based tests with family-wise error correction. Static connectivity yielded no significant group differences in any metric. Dynamic analysis identified six BNS. FES showed a significant increase in the variability of the temporal dynamics and graph-theory features of BNS5, a state characterised by parieto-occipital dominance. The core language network laterality index was significantly reduced in FES within BNS1, a state characterised by auditory-visual dominance. BNS1 occurrence correlated negatively with language disorganisation scores. Dynamic BNS-specific language network metrics correlated with verbal fluency performance exclusively in FES. These findings demonstrate that language dysfunction in early psychosis is expressed as state-dependent disruption of brain network stability and language lateralisation, detectable only through dynamic connectivity analysis.

title: Subanesthetic ketamine modulates region-specific neural and endocrine responses to acute stress in rats.
abstract: Exposure to acute, inescapable stress triggers a coordinated neural and endocrine response across corticolimbic and brainstem circuits. Although subanesthetic ketamine has rapid antidepressant effects, it is unclear whether its modulation of the stress-response network depends on the presence of an acute stressor. In this study, naïve rats received subanesthetic ketamine (15 mg/kg) or a vehicle, and then underwent the tail suspension test (TST) or remained undisturbed in their home cages. Ketamine reduced immobility in the TST and attenuated the stress-induced increase in plasma corticosterone levels. Regional c-Fos expression, ascertained through quantitative real-time PCR and immunohistochemistry, revealed region-specific and context-dependent modulation. Ketamine selectively activated neuronal populations in the prefrontal cortex and potentiated stress-induced activation in the hippocampus and dorsal raphe nucleus. However, it suppressed stress-driven hyperactivation in the amygdala and elicited non-additive activation patterns in the brainstem. These findings suggest that subanesthetic ketamine modulates reconfigures the regional balance of neuronal activation and attenuates hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis reactivity in a state-dependent manner. Furthermore, its effects on the stress-response network are fundamentally influenced by the presence of an acute stressor.

title: Essential Oils From the Fruit of Amomum villosum Lour. Alleviate LPS-Induced Neuroinflammation by Repressing PI3K-Akt and MAPK Signaling Pathways.
abstract: Amomum villosum Lour. has been traditionally valued in various cultures for its health benefits. Here, we show that the neuroprotective effects of the essential oils extracted from the fruit of Amomum villosum Lour. (AVEO) and elucidate its underlying mechanisms in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced neuroinflammation. The main compounds of AVEO can cross the blood-brain barrier and significantly improve cognitive and behavioral dysfunction in LPS-induced mice, leading to a 50% enhancement in Morris water maze performance, a 60% and 80% reduction in immobility time in the tail suspension test and forced swimming test, respectively. Moreover, AVEO mitigates neuron loss and suppresses the expression of pro-inflammatory mediators, including TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6, while upregulating the anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10 in brain tissue. RNA-seq and metabonomics analyses reveal that AVEO modulates multiple inflammation-related pathways and restore metabolic homeostasis in brain tissue. Remarkably, AVEO attenuates hyperactivation of the PI3K-Akt and MAPK signaling pathways in LPS-induced microglia and improves neuronal damage in LPS-induced microglia-neuron co-culture system. Altogether, our findings suggest that AVEO alleviates neural dysfunction by modulating PI3K-Akt and MAPK signaling cascades and promoting metabolic reprogramming upon neuroinflammation, thereby revealing the therapeutic potential of AVEO in several neurological disorders.

title: Interaction with NEGR1 affects mGlu5 cell signalling and the neuroprotection induced by the positive allosteric modulator VU0409551.
abstract: The metabotropic glutamate receptor mGlu5 plays an important role in neuronal survival and synaptic plasticity. We and others have shown that mGlu5 positive allosteric modulators (PAMs) are biased agonists, triggering the activation of neuroprotective pathways and promoting neuronal survival. As mGlu5 biased pharmacology arises from drug-induced interactions with different protein partners, in this study, we analysed the mGlu5 interactome to identify novel binding partners capable of modulating receptor cell signalling. To identify new mGlu5 partners, we employed mass spectrometry, followed by co-immunoprecipitation experiments, which confirmed the interaction between mGlu5 and the neuronal growth regulator 1 (NEGR1), a cell adhesion molecule. We next evaluated how NEGR1 affects mGlu5 cell signalling and cellular distribution using lentivirus transduction on primary neuronal cultures to knockdown NEGR1 expression. We also assessed whether NEGR1 plays a role in the neuroprotective effects of the mGlu5 PAM, VU0409551, by evaluating apoptotic cell death and neurite degeneration. The interaction between NEGR1 and mGlu5 is important for mGlu5 synaptic localization and for its coupling with Homer, thereby modulating cell signalling pathways activated by mGlu5 receptors. For instance, NEGR1 knockdown led to decreased mGlu5-dependent activation of ERK1/2 and reduced expression of ARC/ARG3.1 and BDNF. Importantly, NEGR1 knockdown affected mGlu5 pharmacology, as the neuroprotective effect of VU0409551 was not observed in neurons expressing low levels of NEGR1. These results indicate that NEGR1 is essential for mGlu5-biased activation of neuroprotective cell signalling pathways and for the neuroprotective effects triggered by VU0409551.

title: Instillation timing as the main determinant of aqueous humor nepafenac exposure.
abstract: To evaluate aqueous humor concentrations of nepafenac following topical administration of 0.3% and 0.1% formulations, to assess the influence of timing of instillation on intraocular exposure. Aqueous humor samples collected during anterior segment surgery were analyzed. Nepafenac concentrations were quantified in 151 samples (0.3% instilled once daily: n = 73; 0.1% instilled three times daily: n = 78). Amfenac was quantified only in the nepafenac 0.3% group (n = 73), owing to the stepwise validation of the analytical method (see Limitations). Due to right-skewed distributions, concentrations were summarized as median (IQR) and geometric mean with 95% confidence intervals Mann-Whitney U test and Spearman's rank correlation coefficient were applied. Postoperative optical coherence tomography was performed at 1, 2, and 3 months to assess the occurrence of Irvine-Gass syndrome. Geometric mean nepafenac concentrations were 22.13 nM (95% CI 15.85-30.91) for 0.3% and 21.73 nM (95% CI 13.29-35.53) for 0.1% (p = 0.319). Within the 0.1% group, instillation timing significantly influenced concentrations (p < 0.001), with markedly higher levels approximately 30-60 min after instillation compared with the 10-12 h subgroup. Amfenac correlated with nepafenac (ρ = 0.56, p < 0.001). No cases of clinically evident Irvine-Gass syndrome were observed. No cases of clinically evident Irvine-Gass syndrome were observed; however, the study was not powered or designed to assess clinical efficacy. Timing of instillation is a major determinant of aqueous humor nepafenac concentrations. Preoperative instillation shortly before surgery may optimize intraoperative drug availability and support maintenance of mydriasis. Standardized sampling is essential for robust pharmacokinetic comparisons.

title: Comorbidity patterns and sex differences in late-onset Alzheimer's disease using electronic records.
abstract: In this retrospective study, we applied unsupervised learning techniques to electronic medical records from the University of California, San Francisco (UCSF) to characterize Alzheimer's disease (AD) comorbidity patterns. Given the well-known female predominance in AD, we performed sex-stratified analyses to explore differences in comorbidity patterns based on sex. Findings were evaluated using an independent UC-wide dataset. Among 8,363 patients in the UCSF dataset, we observed five data-driven comorbidity clusters related to cardiovascular conditions, gastrointestinal disorders, and frailty-related conditions such as pneumonia and pressure ulcers, as well as groups with higher and lower overall comorbidity burden. Sex-stratified analyses within clusters identified variation in comorbidity patterns, including circulatory diseases in males in cluster 2 and bladder stones in females in cluster 3. Key results demonstrate partial consistency in the UC-wide dataset. Our study provides a structured characterization of comorbidity heterogeneity in AD and highlights sex-related differences, though findings should be interpreted as descriptive and hypothesis-generating.

title: Dual-Interface Engineering of Cs2CuBiBr6-Based Memristive Synaptic Devices for Neuromorphic Computing.
abstract: Pb-free double perovskite Cs2CuBiBr6 (CCBB)-based resistive random-access memory (ReRAM) synaptic devices are developed using a dual-interface engineering approach to achieve stable resistive switching and neuromorphic functionality. High-quality CCBB thin films are obtained via optimized antisolvent-assisted crystallization, enabling enhanced crystallinity and reduced defect-induced energetic disorder. Modification of the bottom interface with a poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) polystyrene sulfonate (PEDOT:PSS) interlayer improves CCBB film continuity and provides a more favorable environment for homogeneous charge injection. The introduction of an ultrathin bathocuproine (BCP) interlayer at the top interface regulates the spatial redistribution of Ag-related species. The cooperative regulation of charge injection and Ag-related electro-ionic processes promotes more reproducible formation and rupture of localized conductive pathways, resulting in improved switching stability and device-to-device reproducibility. The CCBB-based ReRAM exhibits reliable bipolar resistive switching over 600 cycles, an on/off current ratio of approximately 103, and stable data retention up to 104 s. Gradual and repeatable conductance modulation under electrical pulse stimulation further demonstrates synaptic potentiation and depression behaviors. MNIST-based neural network simulations reveal excellent neuromorphic performance, with up to 90% recognition accuracy. This work highlights cooperative dual-interface regulation of charge injection and Ag-related electro-ionic processes as an effective design strategy for achieving reliable Pb-free perovskite ReRAM and neuromorphic synaptic operation.

title: Real-World Patient Eligibility for Alzheimer's Disease Anti-Amyloid Therapy in Seven Swedish Memory Clinics.
abstract: Anti-amyloid therapies lecanemab and donanemab are the first potentially disease-modifying treatments for Alzheimer's disease (AD) approved in Europe. We estimated real-world eligibility for these treatments in a large multicenter memory clinic patient cohort in Sweden (MemClin). MemClin included patients with a first diagnostic visit between 2016 and 2022 at seven specialist memory clinics in Stockholm, Sweden. To estimate eligibility for anti-amyloid therapy, we applied key inclusion/exclusion criteria from the lecanemab and donanemab appropriate use recommendations. Eligible patients were required to have (1) a clinical diagnosis of AD-type dementia or mild cognitive impairment (MCI), (2) confirmed Aβ pathology (abnormal CSF Aβ42) and (3) no apparent medical exclusion criteria. Eligibility was calculated for different scenarios to provide both upper-bound estimates (main analysis) and more conservative, implementation-ready estimates of near-term treatable patients (sensitivity analysis). Cohort consisted of 2126 patients (mean age 77.1 ± 6.6 years; 61.8% MCI, 24.2% dementia, 13.7% subjective cognitive impairment). In the main analysis, 11.5% of the whole cohort was estimated to be eligible for either treatment (lecanemab 10.6%, donanemab 11.5%). Most eligible patients had early-stage disease (61.9% MCI vs. 38.1% dementia) and an A + T- biomarker profile, that is, normal biomarker of tau (57.9%). Eligibility was markedly lower in sensitivity analyses (e.g., 2.7% when all patients without MRI were assumed ineligible). Even upper-bound estimates indicate that a minority of real-world memory clinic patients may currently qualify for anti-amyloid therapy. These findings provide timely evidence to inform the ongoing debate on the implementation of anti-amyloid therapy in public healthcare.

title: Intranasal administration of enalapril confers acute neuroprotection by mitigating mitochondrial dysfunction and apoptosis in a rat model of ischemic stroke.
abstract: Stroke remains a leading cause of mortality and long-term disability worldwide, with effective treatments hindered by its complex pathophysiology. This study is the first to explore the neuroprotective potential of intranasal enalapril, in mitigating ischemic stroke outcomes through its influence on mitochondrial function. Male Sprague-Dawley rats were subjected to middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO), followed by the intranasal administration of enalapril (0.03 mg/kg) post-ischemia. Neurological function was evaluated after 24 hours of reperfusion through the modified neurological severity score (mNSS), grip strength, and hot plate tests. Brain infarct volume was quantified via Triphenyltetrazolium chloride staining. Blood- brain barrier (BBB) integrity was evaluated via the Evans Blue extravasation assay. Additionally, we employed immunofluorescence techniques to assess apoptosis through TUNEL staining and evaluated mitochondrial function by examining mitochondrial swelling, succinate dehydrogenase activity, mitochondrial membrane potential and reactive oxygen species production. Intranasal administration of enalapril significantly reduced the infarct volume, preserved BBB integrity, and attenuated sensorimotor deficits in MCAO rats. These protective effects were closely associated with enhanced regional cerebral blood flow, a significant reduction in neuronal apoptosis, and improved mitochondrial function. Intranasal enalapril may provide a novel approach to neuroprotection in ischemic stroke, potentially through mechanisms that enhance mitochondrial function and reduce neuronal apoptosis.

title: Placebo effects of caffeine on sport performance: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: A body of research has shown that deceptively administering a placebo described as caffeine can significantly improve sport performance. We aimed to synthesize and estimate the effect size of the deceptive administration of a placebo described as caffeine on sport performance outcomes (e.g. bench press, cycling time-trial, repeated sprint). We searched for studies sampling healthy adults from database creation to July 2026. The standardized mean difference (d) between placebo caffeine and baseline was calculated and Cochrane's risk of bias assessment was used. Seventeen studies were included. Nine studies were judged to be of high-risk of bias and eight unclear. Random-effect models revealed a small-to-moderate effect of placebo caffeine benefiting performance (d = 0.49, 95% CI = 0.28 to 0.69) and meta-regressions indicated that pooled effects were more likely to be greater when researchers were blinded (b = 0.52 ± 0.24, 95% CI = 0.01 to 0.99) and in studies sampling more males (b = -0.93 ± 0.38, 95% CI = -1.68 to -0.19). Data highlight that placebo effects of caffeine can significantly affect sport performance with a pooled effect estimate suggesting a small-to-moderate effect. However, as per the GRADE assessment, the overall quality of evidence was low. As such, given the high risk of bias across all studies and the variation in confidence interval, stronger research designs are needed to examine placebo effects of caffeine, whereby researchers are blinded to treatment administration and allocation concealment. No funding was received for the review and the protocol can be found here: doi: 10.17605/OSF.IO/W8KY6.

title: The Strength of Target Representations Drives Mnemonic Discrimination: Evidence From Extended Delay and Hippocampal Damage.
abstract: Mnemonic discrimination is critical for episodic memory and is dependent on the computational process of pattern separation, which allows the memory system to disambiguate prior memories from potentially overlapping new memories and avoid interference. Prior work with tasks such as the Mnemonic Similarity Task (MST) has demonstrated that discrimination performance is disproportionately affected by hippocampal insult. Further studies have demonstrated that the quality of initial encoding may affect subsequent discrimination performance. Taken together, these results imply that the strength of target memory representations determines discrimination performance in the MST. Here, we manipulated target memory strength by examining MST performance at delays ranging from a few minutes to seven days in three experiments with healthy young adults and a patient with hippocampal damage. Consistent with prior forgetting literature, both target recognition and lure discrimination declined with delay in controls. In the immediate delay condition, the similarity of lures to targets drove discrimination performance, with more similar lures eliciting false alarms and less similar lures eliciting correct rejections, as reflected in the lure discrimination index (LDI). This graded relationship was attenuated or absent at delays longer than one day. However, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses revealed preserved discrimination across delays and target-lure similarity levels. Similarly, the hippocampal patient was impaired relative to controls when considering LDI, but ROC-based analysis revealed intact lure discrimination for the lowest-similarity lures at immediate delays. Finally, we observed an inversion of the typical confidence-accuracy relationship for lure trials at longer delays, with low-confidence responses more likely to be correct for high-similarity lures. Together these findings demonstrate that both the strength of target representations and the degree of lure similarity interact to drive discrimination performance.

title: Neurofeedback for Management of Musculoskeletal Pain: A Randomized Control Trial Using DOMS.
abstract: Chronic musculoskeletal (MSK) pain is associated with maladaptive neuroplasticity, often reflected in altered alpha activity (8-13 Hz). Neurofeedback may offer a way to modulate this activity, yet most protocols target alpha activity during rest, despite movement being a common pain trigger. This study investigated whether neurofeedback during movement could modulate alpha activity and reduce pain in healthy individuals experiencing induced pain via delayed onset muscle soreness (DOMS). This experiment was a randomized, two-armed, parallel-group trial. Twenty-nine participants were included (15 females, mean age = 28 years). Exclusions included neurological, psychiatric, MSK conditions. Participants were randomly assigned to an intervention group (aiming to reduce alpha activity) or a control group (aiming to increase it). Alpha activity was assessed as the alpha power during rest and movement. DOMS was induced using eccentric exercise of muscle extensor carpi radialis in Session 1. Neurofeedback was administered in Session 2, where participants underwent three blocks of neurofeedback training, using individualized EEG-based visual feedback to modulate alpha activity. Session 3 assessed potential lasting neurofeedback effects. Pain was rated across the three sessions, which took place 24-48 h apart. DOMS induction was confirmed by increased pain (p < 0.001, r = 0.82) and reduced alpha activity during movement (p = 0.017, r = 0.49). Neurofeedback did not significantly alter alpha activity (p = 0.114, W = 0.05 for the control group, p = 0.338, W = 0.037 for the intervention group). A single neurofeedback session was insufficient to modulate brain activity or pain perception. Methodological factors, including limited training duration and participants' strategies, may have contributed to the lack of an observable effect. Although neurofeedback did not result in significant changes after one session, the observed alpha modulation following DOMS highlights the relevance of targeting neuroplasticity during MSK pain. Future studies should optimize training protocols and consider multisession designs to enhance clinical applicability.

title: Postoperative delirium and 1-year functional decline, institutionalization and mortality.
abstract: Postoperative delirium is a common and serious complication in older surgical patients and has been associated with increased morbidity, healthcare costs, long-term functional decline and mortality. To determine whether postoperative delirium is associated with functional status, quality of life, institutionalisation and mortality at 1 year after surgery in a large multicentre surgical cohort. Prospective multicentre observational study. Forty-three hospitals in Spain. Surgical patients were recruited in November 2023 and assessed for delirium 48 h after surgery, with follow-up at 1 year. A total of 2442 adult surgical patients undergoing elective or urgent procedures requiring hospital admission. Postoperative delirium was assessed using the Confusion Assessment Method (CAM), CAM for the Intensive Care Unit (CAM-ICU) or the telephone-administered 4AT according to clinical setting. None. Functional status and quality of life at 1 year assessed using the 12-item World Health Organization Disability Assessment Schedule (WHODAS 2.0). Secondary outcomes included institutionalisation and mortality. After excluding 81 deaths and 462 nonresponders, the 1-year telephone follow-up was completed for 1899 patients. Postoperative delirium within the first 48 h was independently associated with a 4.6-point higher WHODAS score at 1 year: adjusted mean difference = 4.60 [95% confidence interval (CI), 1.57 to 7.64, P = 0.003]. Delirium was also associated with increased institutionalisation and higher mortality: odds ratio (OR) 2.5 (95% CI, 1.07 to 5.84, P = 0.03), and (16.7 vs. 3.1%; P < 0.001), including 30-day, 60-day, and 365-day mortality (all P < 0.001), respectively. Postoperative delirium is independently associated with long-term functional decline, loss of independence, institutionalisation and increased 1-year mortality. These findings highlight delirium as a key perioperative complication and support prevention strategies and structured long-term follow-up after surgery. ClinicalTrials.gov (identifier: NC-T06127901).

title: Women With Bipolar Disorder are at Increased Risk of Sarcopenia.
abstract: While bipolar disorder is associated with significant comorbidity, little is known about the musculoskeletal health of individuals with bipolar disorder. Thus, we aimed to investigate the association between bipolar disorder and muscle strength, mass, quality and sarcopenia. Women with bipolar disorder (n = 106) were recruited from healthcare settings and age-matched to controls (n = 300), without bipolar disorder, from the Geelong Osteoporosis Study. Both groups, aged ≥ 20 years. were drawn from South-Eastern Australia. Bipolar disorder was identified using a clinical interview (SCID-I/NP). Maximum handgrip strength (HGS) was measured using a Jamar dynamometer, appendicular lean mass (ALM) using a Lunar densitometer and body mass index (BMI, kg/m2) was calculated. Foundation for the National Institute of Health (FNIH) and European Working Group on Sarcopenia in Older People (EWGSOP2) algorithms were used to determine low HGS, ALM, probable and confirmed sarcopenia. Socioeconomic status (SES) was determined and information on lifestyle obtained via questionnaire. Higher proportion of women with bipolar disorder met criteria for low HGS and ALM compared to those without bipolar disorder. Using FNIH and EWGSOP2 criteria, 36 (8.9%; 34 probable and 2 confirmed) and 46 (11.4%; 43 probable and 3 confirmed) women met criteria for sarcopenia, respectively. Women with bipolar disorder were twice as likely to have sarcopenia (FNIH; OR 2.24, 95% CI: 1.11-4.55 and EWGSOP2; OR 2.78, 95% CI: 1.47-5.20), independent of age, smoking, activity, alcohol, diet and SES. These data suggest women with bipolar disorder have an increased likelihood of sarcopenia. Replication and research into underlying mechanisms are next necessary steps.

title: First seizure referral clinics or first seizure units in neurology: How long is too long?
Early neurocognitive outcomes following SEEG with radiofrequency thermocoagulation.
abstract: Characterization of early neuropsychological outcomes following SEEG with radiofrequency thermocoagulation (RFTHC) is essential to guide patient expectations around return to work, study, and caregiving. The current study aimed to describe the early neurocognitive sequelae of SEEG. Consecutive patients undergoing SEEG were prospectively recruited from two tertiary epilepsy centers in Melbourne, Australia. Patients were administered the Repeatable Battery for the Assessment of Neuropsychological Status (RBANS) via telehealth before and 3 weeks after SEEG (M = 19.69 days, SD = 4.41). Given the telehealth platform, the coding subtest was substituted for the Symbol Digit Modalities Test, and a modified score of global cognitive function was calculated. To evaluate group changes, paired sample t-tests were performed. Reliable change indices were computed to explore individual-level changes. Pearson's correlation coefficients evaluated relationships between change in global cognitive function and SEEG admission variables. SEEG patients were invited to complete a semi-structured interview canvassing the recovery following SEEG. Twenty-eight patients completed the neuropsychological examination (M = 37.89 years, SD = 9.72, range = 17-56 years, 54% female). All patients underwent RFTHC with a mean of 11.43 (SD = 6.87, range = 2-28) coagulation sites. At a whole group level, 3-weeks post SEEG there was no evidence for global nor domain-specific cognitive change. Reliable change indices with 90% confidence revealed only 4% (1/28) declined on at least two measures and 10% (3/28) showed psychometric improvement. Pearson's correlational coefficients showed no evidence for association between change in global cognitive function with SEEG factors including admission length, number of spontaneous or stimulated seizures, number of electrodes, or number of RFTHC sites. Subjective reports of language change tended to be accompanied by a decline on the RBANS language index that did not meet reliable change criteria. Most patients reported returning to work around 4 weeks post SEEG. By 3 weeks, gross cognitive functioning tends to be in keeping with pre-SEEG performances for most patients. These findings have direct clinical implications for SEEG neuropsychological counseling. SEEG is increasingly used to guide epilepsy surgery. Despite this, little is known about the cognitive recovery in the weeks following the procedure. We found that for most patients, broad cognitive functioning 3 weeks after SEEG with coagulation was consistent with function before SEEG, with only a small minority showing significant changes. Some people who reported language difficulties also showed a decline on language testing, although this was often small. Of those patients working before SEEG, most returned to work by 4 weeks. These results provide important evidence to guide patient counseling, recovery planning, and management after SEEG.

title: Design, In Silico Targeting, and Characterization of Curcumin-Ibuprofen Prodrug Microspheres for Brain-Specific Delivery in Alzheimer's Therapy.
abstract: Alzheimer's Disease (AD) is a complex neurodegenerative condition characterized by limited treatment effectiveness, attributed to inadequate Blood-Brain Barrier (BBB) permeability and low medication absorption. Curcumin and ibuprofen possess anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective properties but are limited by pharmacokinetic constraints. This study aimed to synthesize a curcumin-ibuprofen mutual prodrug (CIP), formulate it into chitosan-based microspheres (CIPM), and evaluate its neuroprotective potential for brain-targeted delivery in AD. CIP was synthesized via ethylenediamine carbodiimide (EDCI) mediated esterification and confirmed through IR, NMR, LC-MS, and DSC. CIPM microspheres were prepared using emulsion crosslinking, characterized by scanning electron microscopy, drug entrapment efficiency (85.5%), zeta potential, particle size analysis, and DSC. In silico tools (SwissADME, ProTox-II) and molecular docking were used to assess ADMET profiles and target binding (AChE, BACE1, β-secretase). Network pharmacology identified overlapping targets between curcumin and AD. In vivo evaluation was conducted in a TMT (Trimethyltin)- induced neurodegeneration rat model through behavioral Morris Water Maze (MWM), Novel Object Recognition (NOR), Social Recognition Test (SRT), and biochemical and histological assessments. CIP demonstrated strong binding affinity with AD-related targets (-10.0 to -8.5 kcal/mol) and favorable ADMET properties. Network analysis identified 226 overlapping targets and key hub genes. CIPM significantly improved cognitive performance, antioxidant enzyme levels, and neuronal integrity compared to individual drugs and showed comparable efficacy to donepezil. The present study demonstrates that the curcumin-ibuprofen conjugate, when delivered through chitosan-based microspheres, effectively enhances brain targeting and overcomes pharmacokinetic barriers. The formulation not only improved drug bioavailability but also showed superior neuroprotective and cognitive benefits compared to individual drugs. Molecular docking and network pharmacology further confirmed its multi-target potential, suggesting a synergistic mechanism in modulating key AD pathways. These outcomes highlight CIPM as a promising candidate that warrants further pharmacokinetic and clinical validations for Alzheimer's therapy. The curcumin-ibuprofen prodrug-loaded microspheres present a promising brain-targeted treatment approach for Alzheimer's disease by improving bioavailability, engaging multiple targets, and providing neuroprotection.

title: Ipsilateral Versus Contralateral Femoral Access for Inferior Epigastric Artery Embolization: Impact of Patient Age on Procedural Efficiency.
abstract: Abdominal wall hematomas (AWHs) are relatively uncommon causes of acute abdominal pain but may represent potentially life-threatening vascular emergencies, particularly in elderly patients receiving anticoagulant therapy or in the setting of significant hemorrhage. Transcatheter arterial embolization of the inferior epigastric artery is the recommended first-line therapy. The contralateral femoral approach may be technically demanding in elderly patients with iliac tortuosity, calcifications, or diffuse atherosclerosis. This bicentric retrospective study compared ipsilateral versus contralateral femoral access for inferior epigastric artery embolization, evaluating procedural efficiency, radiation exposure, and clinical outcomes. A bicentric retrospective study included 48 patients treated in emergency settings for epigastric artery bleeding between June 2022 and June 2025. Patients were divided into ipsilateral (n = 23) or contralateral (n = 25) femoral access groups, with further stratification by age (< 60 vs. ≥ 60 years). Technical and clinical success, total angiographic procedure duration, fluoroscopic dose (Air Kerma, mGy), access-site complications, transfusion requirements, rebleeding, and 30-day/3-month survival were analyzed. A subgroup analysis in patients ≥ 60 years (n = 33) assessed the impact of vascular anatomy on procedural metrics. Technical success was 100% in both groups, whereas clinical success was comparable between the contralateral and ipsilateral groups (96.00% vs. 95.65%, respectively). In patients ≥ 60 years, ipsilateral access significantly reduced procedure time (27.90 ± 6.40 vs. 33.30 ± 8.30 min, p = 0.046) and radiation dose (254.00 [IQR 219.00-272.00] vs. 283.50 [IQR 248.80-310.80] mGy, p = 0.023). No major complications or significant between-group differences in rebleeding or survival were observed. In exploratory multivariable analysis, ipsilateral access was associated with lower Air Kerma (β = -56.43 mGy; 95% CI, -91.91 to -20.95; p = 0.002), whereas the adjusted estimate for procedure duration was less precise and did not reach statistical significance. Both femoral access routes are safe and effective. In patients aged ≥ 60 years, ipsilateral access was associated with shorter procedure duration and lower radiation exposure in unadjusted analyses. Exploratory adjusted analyses suggested an association between ipsilateral access and lower radiation exposure, whereas the adjusted association with procedure duration was not statistically significant. These findings require confirmation in larger prospective cohorts.

title: Inside a Programmer's Brain: Dissociating Code and Language Comprehension Networks Using a Novel fMRI-ESM Protocol.
abstract: Code comprehension and natural language share structural similarities but engage partially distinct neural systems. While language predominantly recruits the classical perisylvian language network, code comprehension has been linked to the multiple-demand system, associated with mathematical thinking and problem solving. We report the case of a professional software engineer with an IDH-mutant astrocytoma in the left middle frontal gyrus, a region where these networks converge. To address the potential risk of impairing computer programming abilities during surgery, we implemented a personalized protocol combining fMRI and intraoperative electrical stimulation mapping (ESM), extending the standard language assessment with a Code comprehension task. Intraoperative mapping identified sites in the left inferior frontal cortex that were functionally relevant to the Code comprehension task but were not identified during standard object-naming mapping. Complete tumor resection was achieved while preserving these critical regions, with the patient showing intact post-operative language and programming performances. This single case study suggests that individualized Code comprehension mapping may identify functionally relevant sites not detected by standard object-naming mapping, supporting the potential clinical value of tailored fMRI-ESM protocols for preserving higher-order cognitive functions in neurosurgical patients.

title: Beyond neuroprotection: Context-dependent effects of GLP-1 receptor agonists on seizure susceptibility.
abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are widely used in type 2 diabetes mellitus and obesity and are increasingly considered to exert neuroprotective effects. Recent large-scale clinical and real-world studies report a predominantly neutral to protective association between GLP-1 RA use and seizure- or epilepsy-related diagnoses. However, how these agents affect neuronal excitability in patients with established epileptogenic networks remains insufficiently understood. This narrative review critically examines the experimental and clinical evidence from GLP-1 RA effects on neuronal excitability and seizure susceptibility, with a focus on possible discrepancies between population-level outcomes and individual network-level vulnerability. Preclinical studies demonstrate heterogeneous, network-dependent effects of GLP-1 RAs. Although anticonvulsant and neuroprotective properties are observed in chemically induced seizure models, paradoxical pro-seizure effects occur in genetic absence epilepsy models. In contrast, population-level analyses report neutral to reduced rates of incident epilepsy or seizure-related outcomes under GLP-1 RA therapy. However, these findings are based largely on administrative diagnostic codes, lack epileptological phenotyping, and are not designed to capture transient, exposure-dependent alterations in neuronal excitability or short-term seizure dynamics. Additional factors, including delayed gastric emptying affecting anti-seizure medication absorption, rapid metabolic shifts during titration, blood-brain barrier dysfunction, and agent-specific pharmacokinetics, may further modulate individual susceptibility. We propose that GLP-1 RA effects on neuronal excitability are context dependent, shaped by epilepsy subtype, network vulnerability, exposure dynamics, and treatment phase. Targeted prospective studies incorporating clinical phenotyping, therapeutic drug monitoring, and temporal seizure assessment are required to ensure neurological safety in patients with epilepsy.

title: Symptom-related damage patterns in mesial temporal lobe epilepsy with hippocampal sclerosis.
abstract: This study was undertaken to elucidate the neuroanatomical and network substrates underlying diverse seizure symptoms in mesial temporal lobe epilepsy with hippocampal sclerosis (mTLE-HS) by applying multivariate support vector regression (SVR) to individualized structural symptom mapping and atrophy network mapping (ANM). We retrospectively enrolled 216 patients with mTLE-HS and 460 healthy controls. Six non-mutually exclusive seizure symptoms were assessed. We performed left-right flipping of all images of right-sided mTLE-HS patients along the midline before processing the data. Individual atrophy gray matter maps were derived using normative modeling. Structural symptom mapping was performed using multivariate SVR lesion-symptom mapping. For each patient, indirect ANM maps were generated using a normative functional connectome and direct ANM maps using the patient's own resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging. Correspondence between the two ANM approaches was assessed using individual-level whole-brain spatial correlations of unthresholded maps and group-level Dice coefficients of thresholded maps. Individual structural atrophy patterns were spatially heterogeneous, whereas different seizure manifestations were associated with partially distinct structural patterns and more spatially convergent network-level associations. Focal to bilateral tonic-clonic seizures were associated with thalamic network involvement, gestural/limb automatisms with anterior cingulate-related networks, ictal vocalization symptoms with perisylvian language networks, dysmnesia with hippocampal-posteromedial networks, emotional phenomena with prefrontal-temporal networks, and autonomic phenomena with medial prefrontal and limbic networks. Furthermore, limited spatial correspondence was observed between the results of the direct and indirect atrophy network analyses, suggesting the indirect and direct ANM can be regarded as nonequivalent but potentially complementary approaches. In mTLE-HS, heterogeneous seizure manifestations are associated with distinct patterns of atrophy and distributed functional network involvement. ANM provides a complementary framework for characterizing symptom-related network patterns, and differences between indirect/normative and direct/patient-specific connectome analyses may provide complementary information.

title: CD47-SIRPα Axis as a Target for Neuroprotection.
abstract: Microglial "Off" signaling is crucial for maintaining microglia in a homeostatic state through the interaction of "Off" neuronal ligands with their corresponding microglial receptors. Dysregulation of "Off" signaling has been reported in both acute and chronic neuroinflammation; however, the influence of inflammatory mediators on this pathway remains underexplored. Here, we investigated whether chronic IL-6 or IL-10 overexpression modulates microglia-neuron "Off" signaling after FNA, thereby accounting for the previously observed differences in facial motoneuron (FMN) survival and microglial reactivity in transgenic mouse models (GFAP-IL6Tg and GFAP-IL10Tg). To this end, we examined the expression of the neuronal "Off" ligands CD200, CX3CL1, CD47, and CD22, as well as their corresponding microglial "Off" receptors CD200R, CX3CR1, SIRP-α, and CD45 in non-lesioned and axotomized GFAP-IL6Tg, GFAP-IL10Tg, and WT mice across multiple time points. Our analyses revealed the dynamic regulation of "Off" signaling in both neurons and microglia during microgliosis and FMN phagocytosis and showed temporally restricted strain-specific differences in CD47 expression across genotypes. Chronic IL-6 overproduction promoted a more phagocytic microglial phenotype, defined by downregulation of SIRPα and CX3CR1 alongside upregulated CD45 in the microglial population. In contrast, chronic IL-10 overproduction did not alter the expression of microglial "Off" receptors but induced an IL-10 dependent accelerated upregulation of neuronal CD47. Our findings highlight the CD47-SIRPα axis as a key regulator of FMN death via microglial phagocytosis and emphasize IL-10's neuroprotective potential role through enhanced neuronal CD47 signaling. Overall, this work positions the CD47-SIRPα axis as a potential therapeutic target to mitigate neuroinflammation-induced neuronal loss.

title: Therapeutic and Biomedical Applications of Dopamine-Derived Scaffolds: A Comprehensive Review.
abstract: Dopamine, a pivotal catecholamine, serves as a versatile scaffold in drug design due to its unique pharmacological profile and chemical reactivity. This review integrates evidence on the therapeutic applications of dopamine-derived compounds, ranging from their established roles in treating neurodegenerative disorders such as Parkinson's disease to emerging innovations in enzyme inhibition, gene delivery, and tissue engineering. Furthermore, we discuss structural modifications aimed at enhancing pharmacokinetic properties and brain bioavailability, alongside the utility of dopamine derivatives as molecular tracers in mapping neural architecture.

title: Tactile-Induced Catalepsy for Motor FND: A Feasibility Single-Case Experimental Study and Standardized Protocol.
journal: The Journal of neuropsychiatry and clinical neurosciences
abstract: Functional neurological disorder (FND) is a common and potentially disabling condition for which accessible, evidence-based treatments remain limited. Tactile-induced catalepsy is a novel intervention that temporarily induces increased muscle tone and postural fixation through noninvasive patterned tactile stimulation, potentially facilitating motor retraining. The authors evaluated the feasibility, acceptability, and safety of tactile-induced catalepsy in motor FND. A nonconcurrent multiple-baseline single-case experimental design study was conducted with three adults with motor FND. After a 2- to 4-week baseline phase, participants received 12 weekly sessions of tactile-induced catalepsy delivered by an FND-specialized physiotherapist. Physical functioning was assessed twice weekly by using the physical functioning subscale of the 36-item Short-Form Health Survey. Phase and time effects were analyzed with linear mixed-effects models, supplemented by reliable change indices and minimal clinically important difference thresholds. Two participants showed statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvements in physical functioning during the treatment, and one had a smaller, nonsignificant improvement. No adverse events were reported, and the intervention was feasible to deliver in an outpatient setting. Tactile-induced catalepsy was found to be feasible and associated with improved physical functioning among most participants, supporting further evaluation in larger controlled studies as a potentially accessible and scalable intervention for managing motor FND.

title: Mental Health Symptom Severity Is Positively Associated With Rehabilitation Needs in Veterans and Service Members With Polytrauma, Including Mild Traumatic Brain Injury: A Veterans Affairs Traumatic Brain Injury Model Systems Study.
journal: The Journal of head trauma rehabilitation
abstract: To assess the relationship between rehabilitation needs and mental health symptoms in Veterans and Service Members with polytrauma, including history of mild traumatic brain injury (TBI). Five Veterans Affairs (VA) Intensive Evaluation and Treatment Programs. Veterans and Service Members enrolled in the VA TBI Model Systems study who completed a follow-up greater than 6 months postprogram. Cohort study. Primary regression analyses included rehabilitation needs (Rehabilitation Needs Survey) and post-traumatic stress symptoms (PTSD Checklist-Civilian version). Age, sex, months from rehabilitation to follow-up interview, preinjury mental health, disability level (Glasgow Outcome Scale-Extended), and number of comorbidities were included as covariates. Secondary analyses applied the same model structure to assess the relationship between rehabilitation needs and anxiety (Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7) and depression (Patient Health Questionnaire-9) symptoms. Most Veterans and Service Members with polytrauma, including mild TBI, reported a current need for services to control physical symptoms (55%) and greater than one-third endorsed a current need for services to improve memory (46%), manage emotions (45%), improve health (44%), manage daily stress (42%), and solve daily problems (38%). Adjusted regression analyses revealed that rehabilitation needs were significantly and positively associated with post-traumatic stress, anxiety, and depression self-report symptoms. These relationships were maintained when analyses were repeated with mental health-related items removed from the Rehabilitation Needs Survey, suggesting the finding was not solely because of mental health needs. Higher comorbidity burden and disability were also independently associated with higher rehabilitation needs. Veterans and Service Members with polytrauma, especially those with elevated post-traumatic stress, anxiety, and/or depressive symptoms in the context of mild TBI, could benefit from ongoing access to evidence-based psychotherapies and other specialty care, rehabilitation, and support services to manage long-term care and rehabilitation needs in the chronic phase of injury.

title: Association Between Neighborhood Characteristics and Parent-Reported Lifetime History of Concussion Among Adolescents in the United States.
journal: The Journal of head trauma rehabilitation
abstract: Examine the association between neighborhood characteristics and parent-reported lifetime concussion history. National Survey of Children's Health, a nationally representative survey of parents of children ages 0-17 years in the United States. Parent/guardian(s) (hereafter: parents) with children ages 0-17 years. Cross-sectional. Neighborhood disorder was assessed via items asking whether the child's neighborhood had (1) sidewalks or walking paths, (2) a park or playground, (3) a recreation center/community center/Boys & Girls Club, (4) a library or bookmobile, (5) litter or garbage on the streets or sidewalks, (6) poorly kept or rundown housing, and (7) vandalism such as broken windows or graffiti. Neighborhood cohesion was assessed via items asking whether (1) people in the neighborhood help each other out, (2) neighbors watch out for each other's children, (3) children live in a safe neighborhood, (4) families know where to go for help in the community when difficulties arise, and (5) children are safe at school. Lifetime concussion was assessed with a parent-reported response to a single question. Parent responses for 119 008 children and adolescents (mean age 11.6 years; 48.9% girls) were included. Overall, 5.2% of children and adolescents had a parent-reported history of concussion. The mean neighborhood disorder and cohesion scores were 1.7 (SD = 1.5) and 17.0 (SD = 2.8), respectively. In a multivariable model including both neighborhood disorder and cohesion while adjusting for age, sex, race/ethnicity, household socioeconomic status, past-year sports participation, lifetime ADHD diagnosis, greater neighborhood cohesion was associated with lower odds of lifetime concussion (adjusted odds ratio [95% confidence interval] = 0.96 [0.94-0.98], P < .001). Safer and more supportive built environments, and greater community social cohesion, may help reduce concussion risk. Future longitudinal studies are needed to clarify causal pathways and identify potential community-level intervention targets to reduce concussion risk disparities.

title: A Two-Stage Plasma Biomarker Algorithm Reduces Amyloid PET Use and the p-Tau217 Gray Zone.
journal: Annals of clinical and translational neurology
abstract: Plasma p-Tau217 leaves 30%-50% of patients in an indeterminate "gray zone" often requiring Aβ-PET. We developed GRAD (Gatekeeper-Reflex for Alzheimer's Disease), a two-stage Aβ-positivity prediction model to improve classification while reserving Aβ-PET for residual uncertainty. GRAD was developed in 145 cognitively impaired ADNI participants and externally validated in 1644 cognitively unimpaired A4/LEARN participants. Stage 1 used p-Tau217 alone; probabilities between 0.25 and 0.75 were considered indeterminate. Stage 2 used L2-regularized logistic regression combining plasma-biomarkers, genetic and demographic features. Aβ-PET served as the reference standard (ADNI florbetapir SUVR > 1.11; A4 Centiloid ≥ 20). Full model AUC was 0.915 (95% CI, 0.859-0.961) internally and 0.879 (95% CI, 0.861-0.895) externally. In the external gray zone (n = 630), Stage 2 improved discrimination over p-Tau217 alone (AUC 0.793 vs. 0.719; p < 0.001), increased correct classification without PET from 41.4% to 56.2%, and reduced PET referral from 35.9% to 24.3%. In the p-Tau181 subset (n = 256), Stage 2 outperformed p-Tau181 (AUC 0.799 vs. 0.597; p < 0.001). Overall, 89.0% of ADNI and 90.7% of A4/LEARN participants were classified without PET; modeled testing costs were 44%-52% lower than p-Tau217 screening with PET confirmation of the gray zone. Reflex multimarker testing improves indeterminate p-Tau217 classification while retaining Aβ-PET for residual uncertainty. GRAD may reduce PET use and testing costs in memory-clinic triage, prevention-trial enrichment, and disease-modifying therapy workup.

title: "Controlled by the game"- interviews on why regaining control over gaming is difficult for patients with gaming disorder.
abstract: Research on gaming disorder has grown substantially over the past two decades, but few studies have used qualitative methods. The focus on quantitative studies risks overlooking nuances of gaming disorder. For treatment purposes it is important to have knowledge about the full range of factors maintaining gaming disorder. The aim of this study was to explore how individuals with gaming disorder experience their gaming, with a particular focus on factors that make it difficult to control the amount of time spent gaming. Twelve patients diagnosed with gaming disorder were recruited at an outpatient clinic treating gaming disorder in Gothenburg, Sweden. Semi-structured interviews were conducted to examine factors that hindered them from reducing their gaming. The interviews were transcribed verbatim and analysed using thematic analysis. Thirteen subthemes were identified, forming five main themes: Being committed, Enjoying the game, Filling the void, Climbing an eternity ladder and Being controlled by the game. The themes represent a wide range of reasons why it is difficult to control the amount of gaming, including aspects of the games, individual characteristics of the gamers and their life circumstances outside the games. The results highlight that gaming disorder is multifaceted and maintained by a combination of reduced self-control, structural game characteristics and the fact that gaming satisfies many basic human needs. For clinical purposes, it is important to address game-specific challenges, individual vulnerabilities and factors related to everyday life outside gaming to deliver effective treatments.

title: Childhood-onset parkinsonism, dystonia and severe muscle wasting in a Sudanese girl caused by a novel homozygous DnaJ heat shock protein family (heat shock protein 40) member C6 frameshift variant, with an incidental pathogenic breast cancer 1 gene secondary finding: a case report.
abstract: DNAJC6-related juvenile parkinsonism is a rare autosomal recessive disorder of auxilin, a co-chaperone essential for clathrin-mediated synaptic vesicle recycling. Fewer than 50 kindreds have been reported worldwide, and the condition is easily missed when first-line investigations come back normal. We describe a Sudanese adolescent in whom a previously unreported homozygous DNAJC6 frameshift variant was identified only after a prolonged diagnostic journey that included a period during which her illness was mistakenly attributed to a functional neurological disorder. Clinical whole-exome sequencing additionally returned an incidental medically actionable BRCA1 secondary finding. A 13-year-old Sudanese girl, the eldest child of first-cousin parents, was born preterm and ventilated neonatally for severe respiratory distress. Her development was normal until age five, when an isolated upper-limb tremor first appeared. Over the next 8 years her condition progressed into severe juvenile parkinsonism: bilateral rest-and-action tremor, rigidity, bradykinesia, generalized dystonia with prominent oromandibular involvement, dysphagia, profound cachexia, cognitive and behavioral decline, sleep and autonomic disturbance, episodic oculogyric crises and three discrete seizures. By approximately 11 she was wheelchair-dependent. Earlier, unrevealing investigations had led to a psychiatric diagnosis of functional neurological disorder, and the dopamine antagonists prescribed on that basis worsened her condition. Whole-exome sequencing later identified a novel homozygous DNAJC6 frameshift deletion (NM_001256864.2:c.1480del; p.Glu494ArgfsTer12), absent from population databases, alongside a heterozygous pathogenic BRCA1 deletion reported as an actionable secondary finding. Levodopa produced partial motor benefit, complicated by on-state dyskinesias, visual hallucinations and excessive daytime somnolence. Subsequent up-titration of carbidopa/levodopa to approximately 5-hourly dosing produced a further, clinically evident improvement in gait and fine-motor function. This case adds a previously unreported allele to the DNAJC6 catalog and characterizes the severe end of its phenotype, where corticospinal signs and life-threatening cachexia accompany the more familiar extrapyramidal features. It illustrates the harm that follows premature labeling of a progressive organic movement disorder as functional, especially when dopamine antagonists are then prescribed. The accompanying pathogenic BRCA1 secondary finding shows the dual diagnostic yield that clinical whole-exome sequencing can deliver. Early genetic investigation in childhood-onset movement disorders, particularly with consanguinity, should be the rule, and cascade pathways for actionable secondary findings embedded in routine practice.

title: Neural stem cell transplantation in progressive multiple sclerosis: STEMS study long-term outcomes.
abstract: To evaluate the long-term safety and potential neuroprotective effects of human fetal neural precursor cell transplantation in individuals with progressive multiple sclerosis. This retrospective observational study assessed long-term follow-up data (median 5.7 years) from participants in a first-in-human phase I trial (NCT03269071) investigating neural cell transplantation in progressive multiple sclerosis. Clinical and radiological available data were collected and compared to baseline values and reference populations. Long-term follow-up data were available for 11 of 12 patients. No serious adverse events related to cell transplantation occurred, confirming long-term safety. Although physical disability progressed over time, cognition remained stable compared to baseline. Five patients developed new T2-hyperintense brain lesions without associated contrast enhancement. Long-term gray matter atrophy rates were lower than those observed during the initial two years post-transplantation. Rates of gray and white matter atrophy approximated those of age-matched healthy individuals and patients with early-stage multiple sclerosis, with a trend for a lower atrophy rate compared to a control cohort with progressive disease. These structural findings were consistent with stable levels of circulating biomarkers of neurodegeneration. The findings support the long-term safety of fetal neural cell transplantation in progressive multiple sclerosis. Although exploratory in nature, the stability of cognitive function, reduced brain atrophy, and consistent biomarker profiles support the hypothesis of a possible neuroprotective effect that warrants further investigation in a controlled clinical trial setting.

title: Exome-wide association study reveals common and rare coding variants shaping chronic pain in 327,642 UK biobank participants.
abstract: Chronic pain is a major global health burden with a substantial but incompletely understood genetic basis. Although genome-wide association studies have identified multiple common-variant loci for pain-related traits, the contribution of rare coding variants to chronic pain susceptibility, biological mechanisms, and shared architecture across pain phenotypes remains unclear. We performed an exome-wide association study across ten chronic pain phenotypes using whole-exome sequencing data from 327,642 European participants in the UK Biobank. Variant-level and gene-level association analyses were conducted to identify common and rare coding signals. Downstream analyses included conditional analysis, statistical fine-mapping, validation in non-European populations, replication in independent cohorts, cross-trait meta-analysis, colocalization, pathway and tissue enrichment, single-cell enrichment, summary-data-based Mendelian randomization, and estimation of heritability and genetic correlation from common and rare variants. We identified 286 significant variant-level associations arising from 235 unique variants mapped to 117 genes, including 13 novel lead variants and 44 independent lead signals. Gene-level analyses identified ten significant genes driven predominantly by rare functional variants: ADAMTSL5, ANKRD12, ARID5A, DPP7, GMCL1, HCK, KIF20B, SLC13A1, UBR2, and ZNF558. Functional analyses implicated pathways related to nervous system development, axonogenesis, and synaptic organization, with enrichment in brain tissues and hTRPM8-expressing dorsal root ganglion neurons. Mendelian randomization analyses highlighted convergent regulatory effects across neural and immune-related tissues. Heritability analyses showed that rare coding variants explained a modest proportion of variance relative to common variants but exhibited larger average effects in the most damaging functional classes, particularly high-confidence loss-of-function variants. Genetic correlation analyses revealed shared genetic components among chronic pain conditions and positive correlations with selected psychiatric and nervous system disorders. These findings provide a comprehensive map of coding variation underlying chronic pain and show that both common and rare coding variants contribute to its genetic architecture. Rare coding variants explain only a limited fraction of heritability but offer strong mechanistic insight by implicating discrete genes and pathways related to neuronal development, neuroimmune signaling, and tissue homeostasis. This work advances understanding of chronic pain biology and provides a foundation for future multi-ancestry studies and functional validation.

title: Public brain health: a framework for action to promote and safeguard brain health.
abstract: The promotion of brain health has generally been undertaken at the level of individuals, for instance, in the quest for precision treatments for persons with, or at high risk of, neurological disorders. But the growing global burden of neurological conditions and the increasing understanding of the brain's central role in all facets of human life have spurred interest in public health approaches to the brain that emphasise population-level strategies benefitting everyone as part of a "brain health for all" vision of society. This article defines the emerging concept of public brain health as intersectoral action to establish brain health priorities, empower communities, and reduce health inequities, with the ultimate goal of improving brain health at the population level across the lifetime. We propose a framework to promote and safeguard population brain health with the following key elements: co-defining priorities with communities, balancing prevention strategies, and reducing global gaps in brain health through ambitious policy-making. Public brain health calls for collective responsibility to maximise brain health equity across the life course.

title: De novo formation of familial Alzheimer's disease-relevant Aβ strains occurs exclusively in the human brain.
abstract: In familial Alzheimer's disease (FAD), mutations in the amyloid precursor protein gene (APP) accelerate the aggregation of Aβ peptide, leading to deposition of amyloid plaques within the brain. Conformational variants of Aβ aggregates ("Aβ strains") possess distinct pathological properties and may contribute to disease heterogeneity. While the Swedish APP mutation produces wild-type (WT) Aβ, the Arctic APP mutation generates E22G-mutant Aβ. To clarify whether different FAD mutations are sufficient to specify the formation of distinct Aβ strains, we performed Aβ seeding studies in AppNL-F knock-in mice. Aβ aggregates purified from Swedish and Arctic FAD human brains induced distinct neuropathological signatures, characterized by differences in the morphology and localization of the seeded Aβ deposits, which were preserved upon serial passage. Neither synthetic E22G-mutant Aβ aggregates nor Aβ aggregates isolated from the brains of transgenic mice producing E22G-mutant Aβ recapitulated the phenotype induced by Arctic FAD brain-derived Aβ aggregates upon injection into AppNL-F mice. Similarly, neither synthetic WT Aβ aggregates nor Aβ aggregates from Swedish APP-mutant transgenic mice reproduced the seeding behavior of Swedish FAD brain-derived Aβ aggregates. This suggests that it is the structure of Aβ aggregates rather than the Aβ sequence that dictates seeding activity. We conclude that de novo formation of FAD-relevant Aβ strains occurs exclusively in the human brain, implying the existence of human brain-specific cofactors that modulate Aβ aggregate structure and seeding activity.

title: Neuroepigenetic programming by the maternal environment: part A-epigenome-wide DNA methylation profile in the offspring's olfactory bulb following preconceptional weight loss in mice.
abstract: Experimental models and epidemiological data suggest that the maternal nutritional environment during gestation plays important roles in brain development with consequences on cognitive health. Epigenetic marks, such as methylation and histone modifications, are likely to be involved in this programming, but little addressed the impact of maternal metabolism at the preconceptional period. In mice, we recently demonstrated lasting effects of a maternal preconceptional weight loss on metabolic outcomes and behaviors related to food intake in the male offspring, exhibiting a reduction in olfactory sensitivity, along with a lack of fasting-induced olfactory-based motivation. To evaluate if this effect was driven by epigenetic modifications in the olfactory bulb, we profiled brain DNA methylation, a fundamental process in mediating the relation between early life environment and long-term behaviors in mice according to the maternal status. Using oxidative reduced representation bisulfite sequencing to specifically target 5mC in mice exposed to preconceptional weight loss versus controls, we identified 11,055 differentially methylated cytosines and 150 differential methylated regions (DMRs) located in 111 genes in the olfactory bulb, a main region involved in odor processing and integration. Among the cytosines differentially methylated, half were hypermethylated. Methylation remodeling according to the maternal group preferentially affected noncoding intragenic regions, distal regulatory elements, and open sea CpGs, while promoter CpG islands remain relatively resistant to modification in DNA methylome. The functional annotation of DMRs pointed out genes related to histones kinases, energy signaling, synaptic function, and cellular differentiation, suggesting that targeted methylation changes may simultaneously influence epigenetic regulation, metabolism, and neurobiology. Thanks to a single-base analysis of differential methylated CpGs, we present novel evidence that the maternal dietary environment prior to conception exerts maternally-driven epigenetic effects, markedly altering 5-methylcytosine patterns in the adult offspring brain. This long-lasting remodeling of the offspring's olfactory bulb methylome may underlie the described alterations in olfactory-driven behaviors of offspring born to WL mother.
keywords: Developmental Origins of Health and Disease

title: SLC7A11 suppresses paclitaxel resistance and improves survival via the KLF2 regulatory axis associated with autophagy in ovarian cancer.
abstract: SLC7A11 is well-established as a key mediator of ferroptosis. However, its functional role in regulating autophagy, particularly in the context of ovarian cancer (OC) chemoresistance, remains poorly characterized. Our preliminary results suggested that low SLC7A11 expression is associated with paclitaxel resistance in OC, likely through inhibition of autophagy. Despite this initial observation, systematic functional investigations into the role of SLC7A11 in autophagy regulation and OC chemoresistance are lacking, and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. Therefore, this study aims to elucidate how SLC7A11 mediates chemoresistance in OC through the regulation of autophagy. The effects of SLC7A11 modulation were assessed in paclitaxel-resistant and parental OC cells using functional assays. Autophagy was evaluated via transmission electron microscopy, immunofluorescence, and Western blotting. Autophagy was inhibited using 3-methyladenine or LC3B knockdown. A subcutaneous xenograft model was used for in vivo validation. Clinical relevance was analyzed using patient tissues. Proteomics, bioinformatics, molecular, and CCK-8 assays were integrated to investigate the SLC7A11/KLF2-autophagy axis. SLC7A11 knockdown enhanced the viability of paclitaxel-resistant OC cells (HeyA8-R) following paclitaxel treatment. In contrast, SLC7A11 overexpression sensitized both HeyA8-R cells and their parental HeyA8 cells to paclitaxel, as evidenced by reduced viability, increased intracellular paclitaxel accumulation, and elevated DNA damage. Moreover, SLC7A11 overexpression augmented autophagy-associated activity, and inhibition of autophagy partially attenuated SLC7A11-mediated sensitization to paclitaxel. In vivo studies showed that SLC7A11 suppressed tumor growth and overcame paclitaxel resistance in OC, accompanied by upregulated autophagy-related markers (LC3B, LC3B-II/I, and LAMP1). Mechanistically, SLC7A11 negatively regulated KLF2, a key oncogenic autophagy regulator, and the SLC7A11/KLF2 regulatory axis was associated with LC3B expression and autophagy-associated activity, which may contribute to paclitaxel sensitivity in OC. Clinically, low SLC7A11 expression correlated with chemoresistance and shorter survival in OC. Our findings underscore the significance of the SLC7A11/KLF2-autophagy regulatory axis in OC paclitaxel resistance. They also suggest that SLC7A11 may serve as a prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target for overcoming OC chemoresistance.

title: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy as a tool for monitoring treatment-related neurofunctional changes in posttraumatic stress disorder and trauma-related symptomatology: a narrative review.
abstract: Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is characterized by substantial heterogeneity in symptom presentation, illness trajectory, and treatment response, highlighting the need for objective approaches capable of monitoring treatment-related neurofunctional changes beyond conventional symptom-based outcomes. Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) is an increasingly used non-invasive neuroimaging technique that enables repeated assessment of cortical hemodynamics in clinically feasible settings. Although fNIRS has been widely applied to characterize neurofunctional alterations associated with PTSD, its potential role in monitoring longitudinal treatment-related brain changes has not been critically synthesized. A narrative review was conducted using a structured search strategy across PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, PsycINFO, and the Cochrane Library to identify studies published up to 30 January 2026. Studies were eligible if they included adults with PTSD or clinically significant trauma-related symptomatology and employed repeated NIRS/fNIRS assessments to evaluate neurofunctional changes associated with pharmacological or non-pharmacological therapeutic interventions. Four studies met the eligibility criteria and were included in the qualitative synthesis. Across the included studies, the non-pharmacological interventions consisted of trauma-focused psychotherapy, attention-based cognitive training, and equine-assisted services. No eligible longitudinal studies evaluating pharmacological treatments using repeated NIRS/fNIRS assessments were identified. Across studies, treatment was consistently associated with modulation of prefrontal cortical hemodynamic activity, although the direction and magnitude of neurofunctional changes varied according to intervention type, experimental paradigm, and methodological approach. Overall, the available evidence supports the feasibility of repeated fNIRS assessment while highlighting substantial methodological heterogeneity and the limited maturity of the current evidence base. Current evidence suggests that fNIRS represents a promising and clinically feasible approach for monitoring treatment-related neurofunctional changes in PTSD and trauma-related symptomatology, particularly during non-pharmacological interventions targeting prefrontal regulatory processes. Rather than replacing established neuroimaging techniques such as functional magnetic resonance imaging, fNIRS should be considered a complementary tool that is particularly suitable for repeated assessments in real-world clinical settings. Future research should prioritize adequately powered longitudinal studies, standardized acquisition and analytical protocols, multimodal neuroimaging approaches, and the inclusion of pharmacological treatment trials to determine the potential of fNIRS as a candidate longitudinal neurofunctional biomarker of treatment response. Not applicable.

title: Gonad-soma inter-tissue communication alleviates ultraviolet-induced neurotoxicity in C. elegans.
abstract: Organismal genome stability is constantly challenged by endogenous and exogenous genotoxins, and DNA damage response (DDR) is a classical cell-autonomous mechanism for counteracting such damage. It remains unclear how somatic cells with DDR deficiencies maintain genomic integrity under stress. This study investigated whether inter-tissue communication, particularly from the reproductive system, coordinates DNA damage repair in repair-deficient cells. Using Caenorhabditis elegans, in which certain upstream DDR signaling components are transcriptionally repressed in somatic cells, we examined UV-induced neurotoxicity through behavioral assays (head thrashes, body bends, foraging, and salt chemotaxis). These deficits were associated with preferential impairment of dopaminergic, glutamatergic, and serotonergic reporter readouts, along with heterogeneous transcriptional remodeling of neurotransmitter pathway and pan-neuronal synaptic genes. Deficiencies in upstream DDR signaling (ATM/ATR), whether systemic or germline-specific, significantly exacerbated UV-induced neurobehavioral and transcriptional deficits. In contrast, germline-specific loss of nucleotide excision repair (NER) machinery had no significant effect, highlighting a unique inter-tissue signaling role for upstream DDR. Furthermore, CPR-4 was identified as a key mediator of this inter gonad-soma signaling. Germline DDR activation regulated cpr-4 expression, and loss of CPR-4 abolished UV-induced transcriptional activation of the somatic NER pathway and heightened behavioral sensitivity. Our study revealed a novel germline DDR to somatic tissue signaling axis essential for organismal stress resilience and proposed a new regulatory model centered on gonad-soma signaling.

title: Risperidone for children with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder and severe behavioral dysregulation: a randomized placebo-controlled assessor-blinded trial.
abstract: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a common neurodevelopmental disorder in childhood, and treatment of children with severe behavioral dysregulation remains challenging. This study evaluated the efficacy and safety of adjunctive risperidone specifically in children with ADHD and clinically significant behavioral dysregulation - including irritability, impulsive aggression, and oppositional symptoms - refractory to behavioral intervention alone. In this 48-week randomized, placebo-controlled, assessor-blinded trial, children aged 3-12 years with moderate-to-severe ADHD and significant behavioral dysregulation refractory to behavioral intervention alone were allocated to risperidone (n = 48) or matched placebo (n = 46), both in addition to ongoing structured behavioral intervention and parental psychoeducation. The primary outcome was change in clinician-rated ADHD-RS-IV score from baseline to week 48. Secondary outcomes included parent-rated Conners' scores, Children's Global Assessment Scale (CGAS), treatment response, adverse events, and metabolic parameters. Risperidone produced a significantly greater reduction in ADHD-RS-IV scores than placebo over time (baseline: 28.85 ± 2.62 vs. 28.70 ± 2.50; week 48: 15.63 ± 1.82 vs. 26.47 ± 2.92; p < 0.001). Parent-rated Conners' scores also improved more in the risperidone group (week 48: 16.94 ± 1.81 vs. 28.42 ± 3.04; p < 0.001). Functional improvement was greater with risperidone, with higher CGAS scores and a higher clinical response rate (70.8% vs. 21.7%; p < 0.001). The most common adverse effects were somnolence and increased appetite. Risperidone was associated with greater weight gain and prolactin elevation than placebo, but no serious adverse events occurred. In this study, risperidone was associated with improvement in ADHD symptom severity and global functioning in carefully selected children with ADHD and prominent behavioral dysregulation. However, treatment was also associated with clinically relevant metabolic and endocrine adverse effects. These findings support selective use as a pharmacological adjunct to behavioral intervention in closely monitored patients with significant behavioral comorbidity, and do not justify routine use for uncomplicated ADHD.

title: Mapping the interplay of intelligence, empathy, systemizing, and autistic traits in children with and without autism spectrum disorder.
abstract: Intelligence, empathy, systemizing, and autistic traits are psychological dimensions that vary continuously across the population. Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) may reflect extreme expressions of these traits, yet their interdependencies and difference between typically developing (TD) children remain poorly understood. We recruited 186 children with ASD and 364 TD children aged 6-12 years.
