Intelligence was assessed using the Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children-Fourth Edition, while empathy, systemizing, and autistic traits were measured using validated Chinese versions of the Empathy Quotient, Systemizing Quotient, and Autism Spectrum Quotient. Undirected partial correlation networks and Bayesian networks were estimated separately for each group, adjusting for demographic covariates, including gender, parental education level, and household income. Across groups, cognitive empathy consistently emerged as the central hub in both undirected and Bayesian network analyses. In ASD, autistic traits formed a densely interconnected cluster with limited cross-domain links, while in TD children they were more flexibly integrated with systemizing and other domains. Intelligence formed a cohesive yet relatively independent subnetwork, though in ASD verbal comprehension was directly predicted by social communication competence. The estimated networks demonstrated robust accuracy and acceptable stability. These findings reveal both shared and distinct patterns of network organization among intelligence, empathy, systemizing, and autistic traits in children with and without ASD. Cognitive empathy may represent a potential target for future intervention research, while systemizing tendencies and cognitive strengths may also inform individualized support strategies in ASD.

title: Parabacteroides distasonis ameliorates methylphenidate hydrochloride-induced colonic inflammatory responses and associated gastrointestinal distress.
abstract: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a common neurodevelopmental disorder in childhood, with methylphenidate hydrochloride (MPH) as its first-line pharmacotherapy. Though effective, MPH is associated with underrecognized gastrointestinal adverse events warranting further investigation. Recently, the gut microbiota has attracted attention for treating gastrointestinal distress, but research on its role in alleviating MPH-induced gastrointestinal reactions remains scarce. Herein, Wistar-Kyoto rats (WKY) served as controls alongside spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHR) to explore MPH-induced gastrointestinal adverse drug reactions. The gastrointestinal phenotypes, colonic histopathological characteristics, and inflammatory factor levels were evaluated, and the gut microbiota profiles were analyzed via 16S rRNA gene sequencing. The protective effect of Parabacteroides distasonis (P. distasonis) was further verified by supplementing the treated rats with this strain. We demonstrated MPH induced diarrhea and colonic inflammatory responses in rats. 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing revealed that MPH-treated rats had significantly decreased gut microbiota health index, increased dysbiosis index, and reduced P. distasonis abundance, suggesting MPH-induced gastrointestinal reactions may correlate closely with reduced P. distasonis. Further experiments confirmed that P. distasonis supplementation effectively alleviated diarrhea and colonic inflammatory responses in MPH-treated rats. Collectively, this is the first study verifying that P. distasonis supplementation mitigates MPH-induced gastrointestinal adverse reactions, providing a novel intervention strategy to improve tolerance of ADHD pharmacotherapy.

title: Dexmedetomidine-based opioid-sparing anesthesia in video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery: a randomized controlled trial.
abstract: Dexmedetomidine has increasingly been incorporated into opioid-sparing anesthetic strategies during video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) because of its analgesic properties and minimal respiratory depression. However, dexmedetomidine remains associated with dose-related hemodynamic adverse effects, particularly bradycardia and hypotension. We evaluated whether a reduced-dose dexmedetomidine regimen decreases intraoperative opioid requirements while maintaining acceptable hemodynamic safety during VATS. In this prospective randomized controlled trial, 68 patients undergoing VATS were randomly assigned to either a dexmedetomidine group or a control group (34 patients each). The dexmedetomidine group received a loading dose of 0.5 µg/kg followed by continuous infusion at 0.5 µg/kg/h during surgery. The control group received conventional fentanyl-based anesthesia. The primary outcome was maintenance-phase rescue fentanyl consumption. Secondary outcomes included postoperative pain scores, postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV), postoperative respiratory complications, and perioperative safety outcomes. Maintenance-phase rescue fentanyl consumption was significantly lower in the dexmedetomidine group than in the control group (18.7 vs. 33.2 µg, P = 0.009). Postoperative pain scores, rescue analgesic requirements, PONV, and respiratory complications were comparable between groups. However, the dexmedetomidine group demonstrated a higher incidence of intraoperative bradycardia (23.5% vs. 0%, P = 0.005) and postoperative hypotension during PACU stay (23.5% vs. 2.9%, P = 0.027). These hemodynamic events were transient and responsive to pharmacologic intervention. Dexmedetomidine-based opioid-sparing anesthesia reduced maintenance-phase rescue fentanyl administration during VATS. However, the reduction was modest, was not associated with clear postoperative benefits, and was accompanied by increased bradycardia and hypotension. ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05431322), registered on 14 June 2022. Available at https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05431322 .

title: A single-cell atlas of intracranial aneurysm progression identifies a dysfunctional VSMC subpopulation associated with rupture risk.
abstract: Intracranial aneurysm (IA) rupture is a life-threatening event. While inflammation is implicated, the cellular mechanisms associated with progression from stable lesion to rupture remain poorly defined at single-cell resolution. We performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) on a mouse model spanning sham, formed, and ruptured IA stages. Computational analyses included trajectory inference, cell-cell communication analysis, and metabolic scoring. Key findings were validated using human IA bulk RNA-seq data and protein-level assays on matched clinical tissues. Our single-cell atlas revealed a progressive "inflammatory-lytic" microenvironment marked by immune cell infiltration and vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) depletion. We identified a metabolically specialized VSMC subpopulation (VSMC_0) that was selectively lost in formed and ruptured aneurysms. Pseudotime analysis indicated VSMC differentiation blockade, associated with downregulation of the structural genes actin alpha2, smooth muscle (ACTA2) and prolyl 4-hydroxylase subunit alpha2 (P4HA2), which correlated with irregular aneurysm shape a strong clinical predictor of rupture risk. Cell communication analysis positioned VSMC_0 as a signaling hub to macrophages, suggesting a feed-forward inflammatory loop. These findings were validated in human IAs tissues. Our study identifies VSMC phenotypic dysregulation as a key correlate of IA instability, linking molecular deficits to clinical rupture predictors. This reframes IA as a disorder of vascular cellular identity and communication, revealing potential therapeutic targets for aneurysm stabilization.

title: Comparison of dexmedetomidine and droperidol-fentanyl for asleep-awake-asleep techniques in awake craniotomy anesthesia: a randomized controlled study.
abstract: In this study, we aimed to compare dexmedetomidine with droperidol-fentanyl during the intraoperative awakening phase of awake craniotomy (AC), focusing on wake-up time. We conducted a single-center randomized controlled trial in China from January 2018 to December 2018. Patients aged 36-60 years, with American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status I-II, scheduled for brain glioma resection, were screened for eligibility; 61 were randomized, and 60 were included in the final analysis. The patients were randomized to either the dexmedetomidine group (intravenous loading dose of dexmedetomidine 0.5 µg·kg- 1 after discontinuation of propofol and remifentanil, followed by a maintenance infusion of dexmedetomidine 0.3-0.5 µg·kg- 1·h- 1) or the droperidol-fentanyl group (intravenous loading doses of fentanyl 2 µg·kg- 1 and droperidol 5 mg after discontinuation of propofol and remifentanil, followed by continuous maintenance infusions of fentanyl 2 µg·kg- 1·h- 1 and droperidol 0.1 mg·kg- 1·h- 1). A wake-up assessment was performed during maintenance of the assigned study regimen. The primary outcome measure was wake-up time. Secondary outcomes included the Observer's Assessment of Alertness/Sedation (OAA/S) scale, Numerical Rating Scale (NRS), eloquent brain area mapping status, vital signs, and adverse events. Baseline characteristics were comparable between the groups. Compared with the droperidol-fentanyl group, the dexmedetomidine group had lower mean arterial pressure at T4-T7, lower heart rate at T1-T4 and T7, and a shorter wake-up time, with a between-group difference of 3.5 min (95% CI, 1.95 to 5.05; P < 0.001). No statistically significant differences were detected in OAA/S scores at wake-up (T2), NRS scores, eloquent area mapping status, or adverse events between the groups. No statistically significant differences were detected in OAA/S scores at wake-up or intraoperative brain mapping performance between the two groups. The dexmedetomidine regimen was associated with a shorter measured wake-up time. The Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR1800014329) was retrospectively registered on 6 January 2018.

title: Automated Magnetic Resonance Volumetry to Measure Multiple System Atrophy Disease Progression in Clinical Trials.
journal: Movement disorders : official journal of the Movement Disorder Society
abstract: Recent studies have reported longitudinal brain atrophy in multiple system atrophy (MSA) in relatively small patient cohorts. To compare longitudinal regional brain volume and clinical changes as endpoint measures for MSA clinical trials. MSA patients with 1-year longitudinal brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) were selected from the placebo arm of the M-STAR Study (NCT03952806) and stratified into MSA-cerebellar (MSA-C) and MSA-parkinsonism (MSA-P) subtypes. A multisite healthy control (HC) cohort from international datasets was included for comparison. Baseline and longitudinal atrophy were assessed through automated MRI volumetry. Standardized longitudinal effect size values with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) and sample sizes required to detect treatment effect were estimated for 42 individual regional brain volumes, four combined volumetric indexes, nine clinical scales, and serum neurofilament light chain. The final study cohort included 129 MSA patients (76 MSA-C, 53 MSA-P) and 184 HC. The most atrophic structures at baseline were infratentorial regions in MSA-C and putamen in MSA-P. In both subtypes, infratentorial structures showed the largest longitudinal volume loss compared with HC. The annualized change of a cerebellum-pons-putamen volumetric index was the most powerful progression biomarker in MSA patients (effect size: -1.81 [95% CI: -2.14, -1.55]) and in both subtypes (MSA-C: -2.04 [95% CI: -2.58, -1.68], MSA-P: -1.55 [95% CI: -2.08, -1.22]), requiring the lowest sample size per arm (MSA, N = 55 to detect 30% treatment effect), and outperforming clinical measures (-59.6% patients required per arm). These findings support longitudinal MRI-derived regional atrophy rates as sensitive imaging endpoints to assess treatment efficacy in MSA clinical trials. © 2026 The Author(s). title: Decision dynamics of negative bias in subclinical depression during ambiguous facial emotion perception.
abstract: Individuals with depressive tendencies may categorize ambiguous facial expressions toward negative rather than happy endpoints, but the associated decision-process components remained unclear. The study examined whether the categorization shift was associated with differences in perceptual criterion, discrimination sensitivity, response dynamics, or diffusion-model parameters. Fifty-nine participants, comprising a depressive tendency group and a comparison group, categorized morphed Sad-Happy and Angry-Happy expressions presented in a 750-ms face/mask sequence or a 1500-ms face/no-mask sequence. Psychometric functions, area-under-the-curve (AUC) analyses, quadratic mixed-effects models of response time, and a hierarchical drift-diffusion model were applied. Across conditions, the depressive tendency group showed lower points of subjective equality than the comparison group, indicating a relative shift in the categorization boundary toward the negative versus happy endpoint, without a corresponding group difference in discrimination sensitivity. AUC analyses similarly indicated higher negative-response probabilities in the depressive tendency group, particularly within the low-negativity portion of the continuum. Condition-specific patterns were observed, but direct tests did not support a larger Sad-Happy group difference in the 1500-ms than in the 750-ms presentation sequence. In the focal Sad-Happy 1500-ms face/no-mask sequence, the selected drift-diffusion model indicated a group-related drift-criterion shift toward the Sad boundary and modestly longer non-decision time in the depressive tendency group, whereas starting-point bias and boundary separation did not differ between groups. These findings are consistent with a relative categorization shift toward negative versus Happy facial-expression endpoints among participants with depressive tendencies. The diffusion-model results provided a model-dependent account of the focal choice-response-time pattern under the present presentation-sequence structure.

title: Altered brain function and its spatial correlations with neurotransmitter maps in anterior shoulder pain patients.
abstract: Neuroimaging studies have reported that chronic pain may be associated with brain functional changes and related molecular mechanisms. However, there are few studies in anterior shoulder pain (ASP). Thus, we aimed to assess the possible brain functional changes and their associations with neurotransmitter receptor maps in ASP patients. Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging data were obtained from 27 ASP patients and 20 healthy controls (HCs). Regional homogeneity (ReHo) and fractional amplitude of low-frequency fluctuation (fALFF) methods were used to examine altered brain functions. JuSpace toolbox was employed for evaluating the spatial correlations between ReHo and fALFF changes and neurotransmitter receptor maps. Regression analysis was conducted to explore the associations between neuroimaging findings and clinical characteristics in ASP patients. Furthermore, we investigated reliable biomarkers to distinguish ASP patients from HCs using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. ASP patients had abnormal ReHo/fALFF in the middle temporal gyrus, putamen, caudate, pallidum, precentral gyrus, medial prefrontal cortex, precuneus, posterior cingulate cortex and inferior temporal gyrus. ReHo/fALFF alterations in ASP patients were associated with the serotonin, dopamine, GABA, choline, glutamate and norepinephrine neurotransmitter systems. Visual analog scale was positively correlated with ReHo in the right insula. Moreover, ROC analysis showed higher classification accuracy in the middle temporal gyrus, precentral gyrus and putamen. Our study investigated abnormal brain function and associated neurotransmitter receptor maps in ASP patients, which may contribute to improving our understanding of the pathophysiological mechanisms in ASP.

title: Carbon-12 and Gamma-Rays Combined Irradiation Ameliorates Behavioral and Biochemical Alterations in Tau P301S Homozygous Transgenic Mice.
abstract: No effective treatments currently exist for tauopathies. Given emerging evidence that moderate-dose ionizing radiation (IR) may exert neuroreparative effects in neurodegeneration, we investigated the impact of combined IR exposure on disease progression in the Tau P301S mouse model. Tau P301S mice received combined gamma-ray (0.24 Gy) and carbon-12 nuclei (0.18 Gy, 400 MeV/n) irradiation at the presymptomatic stage. Following longitudinal behavioral testing until the terminal stage, post-mortem brains were analyzed via RT-qPCR, ELISA, and HPLC to assess gene expression, protein levels, and monoamine quantification. At the symptomatic stage, Tau+R mice showed normalized endurance, fear-dependent memory, and disinhibition-like behavior, reaching wild-type levels. At the terminal stage, Tau+R mice demonstrated significantly superior balance, coordination, and grip strength compared to untreated Tau P301S mice. These benefits correlated with restored striatal serotonin and a 76% reduction in cerebellar tau protein (transcription-independent). Furthermore, IR normalized Gsk3b expression in the hippocampus and cerebellum, and Trem2 in the cerebellum, to WT levels. Notably, IR up-regulated cerebellar Iba1 by 31% and 86% compared to WT and Tau mice, respectively. Combined radiotherapy not only alleviates behavioral symptoms but also modulates key neurochemical parameters. These findings demonstrate robust symptomatic improvements and suggest a potential neuroprotective capacity of combined radiotherapy in a mouse model of severe tauopathy.

title: Meprin β is specifically inhibited by its cognate synthetic propeptide.
journal: Cellular and molecular life sciences : CMLS
abstract: Meprin β is a zinc-dependent metalloprotease of the astacin family highly expressed in kidney and intestine. Dysregulation of meprin β expression and activity was observed in several pathological conditions such as Alzheimer's disease, cancer, fibrosis, and inflammatory bowel disease. Therefore, inhibition of meprin β could be a promising therapeutic option to treat pathological conditions influenced by this protease. However, available small-molecule compounds such as the broad-spectrum metalloproteinases inhibitors marimastat or actinonin lack specificity. Hence, more selective meprin β inhibitors needs to be developed. Here, we provide evidence that the synthetically generated cognate meprin β propeptide serves as highly specific inhibitor for the protease (IC50 = 1.35 µM), while other related metalloproteases such as meprin α and a disintegrin and metalloproteinases (ADAMs) are not affected. Employing a targeted approach revealed that removal of the last four C-terminal amino acids of the propeptide significantly improved its inhibitory capacity (IC50 = 0.68 µM). In cell-based experiments, treatment with the propeptide resulted in diminished meprin β activity and decreased cleavage of its substrates, including the interleukin-6 receptor (IL-6R) and the G protein-coupled receptor latrophilin-3 (LPHN3). Suitability was further confirmed in ex vivo cultivated organotypic brain slices, where the administration of the propeptide also resulted in decreased meprin β activity and diminished latrophilin-3 cleavage. Thus, not only the synthetic wildtype propeptide but especially a C-terminally truncated propeptide of meprin β represent highly specific inhibitors with potential for therapeutic application.

title: ASIC1a as an integrating node in ischemic neurotoxicity: crosstalk with NMDAR and TRPM signaling.
journal: Pflugers Archiv : European journal of physiology
abstract: Ischemic stroke triggers acidosis, glutamate excitotoxicity and oxidative stress, which converge to disturb ionic homeostasis through several cation channels, including acid-sensing ion channel 1a (ASIC1a), N-methyl-D-aspartate receptors (NMDARs) and transient receptor potential melastatin (TRPM) channels. Emerging evidence suggests that ASIC1a functions as a context-dependent integrating node: protons directly gate ASIC1a, glutamate and bilirubin-associated signaling can modulate ASIC1a-dependent injury pathways. ASIC1a directly couples with NMDAR-dependent signaling and indirectly engages TRPM-associated pathways. Here, we discuss the mechanistic basis, therapeutic potential and unresolved questions regarding ASIC1a-associated signaling in ischemic brain injury.

title: An amygdala-mediated simulation-to-decision cascade aligns interbrain dynamics to solve social dilemmas.
abstract: Mutual cooperation (MC) requires independent decision-makers to coordinate under uncertainty about each other's intentions. Using simultaneous intracranial electroencephalography from epilepsy-patient dyads playing a real-time iterated prisoner's dilemma, we identified neurocognitive mechanisms that enable interacting brains to align during mutual cooperation. Amygdala interbrain representational alignment (IBRA), similarity in fine-grained neural spectral patterns across partners, emerged selectively during MC and predicted trial-by-trial outcomes. Early θ-suppression-characterized IBRA reflected rapid, history-sensitive alignment, whereas later IBRA, characterized by low-frequency suppression and γ increases, supported coordinated commitment and action. Furthermore, mutual cooperation relied on an amygdala-mediated, simulation-to-decision cascade, operationalized here as a model-based prospective estimate of partner cooperation that guided self-choice. Amygdala low-frequency suppression tracked this prospective estimate of partner cooperation and θ-γ coupling linked this partner estimate to self-decision processes. Conditional cooperators strategically relied on partner tracking, whereas unconditional cooperators leveraged dispositional tolerance of uncertainty to transition into anticipatory neural alignment. These findings reveal the neural interdependency underpinning MC, redefining cooperation not as isolated decision-making but as a dynamic, interbrain, cognitive alignment.

title: Spatiotemporal remodeling in habenula marks the onset of depression-related phenotypes.
abstract: Chronic stress has lasting adverse consequences that can lead, over time, to depression, yet the optimal timeframe for effective therapies remains unclear. The lateral habenula (LHb) has been implicated in stress-related behavioral repercussions, but the precise timing of its contribution is not understood. Here, using spatial transcriptomics, we generated a spatially resolved molecular atlas of the LHb of male mice, revealing a topographically organized and temporally defined remodeling of gene expression after chronic stress. Longitudinal in vivo two-photon calcium imaging of individual LHb neurons revealed progressively heightened excitatory responses to aversive stimuli. These neuronal adaptations mirrored both the progression of transcriptional changes and the emergence of depression-related behavioral phenotypes and were reversed by the antidepressant ketamine. Moreover, chemogenetically limiting LHb neuronal activity or administering ketamine at the onset of these changes exerted antidepressant effects. These findings link spatiotemporal signatures of LHb neuronal ensembles and genetic landscape with the onset of stress-induced depression-related states.

title: Three reasons why AI is not conscious and perhaps never will be.
The molecular footprint of valproic acid in human hippocampal organoid.
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a multifaceted neurodevelopmental condition characterized by neuroinflammation, and disruption in neuronal development. Valproic acid (VPA) is a known environmental risk factor for ASD. Induced pluripotent stem cells (IPSCs IMR90-4)-derived human hippocampal organoids (hHOs) at 60 days of development were used to investigate VPA-induced changes in mRNA and microRNA (miRNA) profiles. The molecular effects of VPA on hHOs were deciphered by meaningfully integrating the ability of miRNA to regulate expression of their predicted mRNA targets crucial to altering neuroinflammatory pathways. Molecular footprint can be defined as the VPA-induced changes to the miRNA profile resulting in coordinated post-transcriptional (mRNA) regulation of neuronal and inflammatory pathways associated with ASD. Based on the results, the molecular footprint of VPA in hHOs was generated for the first time. These findings highlight the contribution of miRNA-mediated regulatory mRNA networks to VPA-induced neuroinflammation-associated with ASD in hHOs.

title: Memory stays strong in old age when this brain enzyme is active.
